blindSummary:
This is a relatively safe destination with a notably more conservative climate and a live far-right government hostility signal. The senior governing far-right party mocks gender-diverse people publicly and has pledged a constitutional "two sexes" definition that would repeal non-binary protections — a threat, not yet enacted.

The most concrete traveler-relevant risk is organised dating-app predation: in 2025 authorities uncovered a neo-fascist network that lured, beat, humiliated and filmed victims — primarily gay and bisexual men — through fake dating profiles (15 arrested). Caution is warranted on dating apps for queer travelers. There is no bathroom restriction law, no cross-dressing statute, and no documented border-police humiliation of trans travelers.

If detained, there are no specific legal protections for trans detainees — they are housed with the general population on an ad-hoc basis (only three trans people were in detention as of mid-2025). Trans-specific hate incidents actually declined in 2025, though homophobic violence rose.
blindOutOfScope: General urban crime is low; the high cost of living is a non-safety travel note.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2026 (covering 2025), chapter on this country. Documents a neo-fascist network uncovered in March that used fake dating profiles to lure gay and bisexual men to ambushes by masked assailants (attacks filmed and shared); a rejected capital-city petition for queer sauna time slots; new education-ministry rules restricting outside sex-education providers; and ombuds-office guidance for gender-inclusive forms for intersex and non-binary people.

Research-institute national report (2025) on LGBTIQ detainees in this country, part of a regionally funded project. Covers the legal framework for LGBTIQ people in detention, gender self-determination, anti-discrimination protection, and the situation and rights of LGBTIQ people in this country's prisons.

National parliament document (May-June 2025): the justice ministry's answer to a parliamentary question on the placement of transgender persons in this country's penal institutions - official information on how trans inmates are housed.

Foreign broadcaster (March 2025): police arrested 15 people (aged 14-26) over a wave of hate attacks in which at least 17 LGBTQ people were lured via fake dating-platform accounts to remote locations, ambushed by masked groups, filmed, and falsely accused of being paedophiles. Investigators believe the real victim count is much higher.

Local news outlet (July 2026): this country recorded 6,751 suspected hate crimes and 7,327 prejudice motives in 2025, with 1,575 victims of prejudice-related violence; police data broken down by who faces violent hate crime, while acknowledging under-recording.
An LGBTQ+ organisation's news site (Jul 2026): official hate-crime statistics for this country show homophobic offences rising while transphobic incidents declined over the reporting year.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Sept 2024): this country's far-right party won the most votes in a national election for the first time in the postwar era (29.2%), raising concerns about what a far-right-led government could mean for LGBTQ+ people.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity legal since 1971, marriage equality since 2017, full adoption rights since 2016. Legal gender recognition is possible without mandatory medical procedures, and individuals may obtain an 'X', indeterminate, or no gender marker; intersex people can choose an additional legal designation beyond the binary, or none at all. The equal-treatment law covers sexual orientation, with recent amendments broadening 'gender' to include gender identity, expression and sex characteristics.
NOTE: this is an antifascist monitoring-platform page documenting far-right incidents in this country; its content is about far-right extremism generally, not specifically about trans or LGBT issues.

Report 2025/2026 by the country section of an international human-rights organisation: covers cost-of-living, gender-based violence, restricted abortion access, freedom-of-assembly risks, inadequate anti-discrimination law, and police not required to wear ID badges. General human-rights context, not trans-specific.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (May 2019): this country recognised a third gender option in official documents - an intersex activist received the country's first non-binary passport ('X' marker) and birth certificate (a new third designation), following the June 2018 constitutional-court ruling that gender identity must be accurately reflected in official documents; the interior ministry restricted the new designation to people with a medical panel certificate of intersexuality.
blindLocalsOnly: Legal gender recognition runs through the courts (the constitutional court affirmed gender identity as protected in December 2025) — a resident-facing process.
blindTangential: The dating-app predation network targeted gay and bisexual men primarily — a risk for trans visitors using apps, though not trans-specific.
